title: Socratic checklist — reproducibility & freezing (复现与冻结)
rationale: Reproducibility is a cross-stage constraint, checked at least twice: at the Stage 6 freeze and again at Stage 8 reporting. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Is the analysis input frozen (data file, config, seed, model checkpoints) with SHA-256 hashes recorded before any result is derived?
items.rationale: Without an input freeze, results cannot be regenerated bit-for-bit and no audit is possible.
items.answer_format: freeze manifest: artifact list + hash + timestamp

items.question: Is the analysis code versioned at a specific commit, and does the receipt record that commit plus the runtime versions (R/Python, packages, OS-level notes)?
items.rationale: Code without version pins reproduces nothing; package drift is the usual failure.
items.answer_format: commit hash + sessionInfo()/pip freeze + env lock file path

items.question: Can a clean-machine re-run regenerate every headline number from the frozen inputs, and has at least one full re-run been executed and logged?
items.rationale: A reproducibility claim is an execution result, not a promise; at least one cold re-run must exist.
items.source: MetaWingman re-run norm (time-split reconstruction target); PRISMA 2020 item 27
items.answer_format: re-run log + diff between original and regenerated outputs

items.question: Is the RNG seeding explicit for every stochastic step (sampling, imputation, simulation, model training) and recorded in the receipt?
items.rationale: Unseeded stochastic steps are the most common silent non-reproducibility.
items.source: MetaWingman seed convention (20260815); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.10 (analysis)

items.question: Are intermediate objects (per-stage data, model checkpoints, review files) saved at each stage boundary so any single stage can be re-run without redoing the whole pipeline?
items.rationale: Stage-level resumability is the practical definition of a reproducible pipeline.
items.source: MetaWingman stage norm (receipts at every stage); PRISMA 2020 item 27
items.answer_format: artifact map per stage + restore instructions

items.question: Is the data lineage recorded from raw export to analysis table, including every transformation (dedup, merge, conversion) with code and parameters?
items.rationale: Raw-to-analysis lineage is what lets a reviewer verify that no study was silently lost or altered.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 items 3, 16a-16b (counts and flow); MetaWingman lineage norm
items.answer_format: lineage log: input -> transform -> output per step, with counts

items.question: Are all learned components (trained models) archived with their training receipts, data splits, and the exact commit of the training script?
items.rationale: A checkpoint without its training receipt is a black box; the receipt is the scientific record.
items.source: MetaWingman component preregistration norm (appraisal-step preregistration as template)
items.answer_format: per-component: checkpoint hash + receipt path + split definition + script commit

items.question: Is the time-split reconstruction check planned or executed: can the current pipeline reproduce a past review's numbers when pointed at its frozen inputs?
items.rationale: Reconstruction against known past reviews is the strongest end-to-end reproducibility evidence.
items.source: MetaWingman VAL-2 plan (time-split reconstruction as the current bottleneck item)

items.question: Are raw data files preserved read-only with a documented no-overwrite policy, and derived outputs written only to separate results directories?
items.rationale: Overwritten raw data destroys provenance silently; separation is the structural fix.

items.question: Which single stage of the pipeline is currently the weakest reproducibility link, and what is the concrete fix?
items.rationale: Naming the weakest link turns reproducibility from a slogan into a work queue.
